hints: Clear denominators, compare coefficients, and verify both constants by recombination.
walkthrough:
Factor the denominator of $\dfrac{2}{1 - 9y^2}$ as a difference of two squares:
$$1 - 9y^2 = (1 + 3y)(1 - 3y)$$
$$\dfrac{2}{1 - 9y^2} = \dfrac{A}{1 + 3y} + \dfrac{B}{1 - 3y}$$

Clear denominators to set up the identity for all $y$:
$$2 = A(1 - 3y) + B(1 + 3y)$$

Substitute $y = \dfrac{1}{3}$ to find $B$:
$$2 = A\left(1 - 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right) + B\left(1 + 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right) \implies 2 = A(0) + B(1 + 1) = 2B \implies B = 1$$

Substitute $y = -\dfrac{1}{3}$ to find $A$:
$$2 = A\left(1 - 3\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right) + B(0) \implies 2 = A(1 + 1) = 2A \implies A = 1$$

ai_rubric.Partial Fractions: Derives $A=1,B=1$. Concludes with $\dfrac1{1+3y}+\dfrac1{1-3y}$. The final result is $\dfrac1{1+3y}+\dfrac1{1-3y}$.

hints: Separate the variables and use part (a) to integrate the y-side to (1/3)ln((1+3y)/(1−3y)).
Integrate the x-side to a tan3x term and apply the stated initial condition to determine the constant.
Exponentiate, solve the resulting ratio equation for y, and simplify to an explicit expression in x.
walkthrough:
Use the partial fractions from part (a) to integrate the left-hand side:
$$\int \left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 3y} + \dfrac{1}{1 - 3y}\right)\,\mathrm{d}y = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(1 + 3y) - \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(1 - 3y) = \dfrac{1}{3}\ln\left(\dfrac{1 + 3y}{1 - 3y}\right)$$

Integrate the right-hand side with respect to $x$:
$$\int \sec^2(3x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan(3x) + C$$

Use the boundary condition $y = 0$ when $x = \dfrac{1}{12}\pi$ to evaluate $C$:
$$\dfrac{1}{3}\ln\left(\dfrac{1 + 0}{1 - 0}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan\left(3 \times \dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) + C$$
$$\dfrac{1}{3}\ln(1) = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + C \implies 0 = \dfrac{1}{3}(1) + C \implies C = -\dfrac{1}{3}$$
$$\dfrac{1}{3}\ln\left(\dfrac{1 + 3y}{1 - 3y}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\tan(3x) - \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Multiply through by 3 and exponentiate both sides:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{1 + 3y}{1 - 3y}\right) = \tan(3x) - 1$$
$$\dfrac{1 + 3y}{1 - 3y} = \mathrm{e}^{\tan(3x) - 1}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Integrates $2/(1-9y^2)$ to derive $\frac13\ln(1+3y)-\frac13\ln(1-3y)$. Derives term $\frac13\tan3x$. The final result is $y=\dfrac13-\dfrac{2}{3(1+e^{\tan3x-1})}$, equivalently $y=\dfrac{e^{\tan3x-1}-1}{3(e^{\tan3x-1}+1)}$.
